articles.title: Gray Media Closes $600 Million Term Loan And Extends $680 Million Revolver
articles.snippet:
Gray Media closed a new $600 million Term Loan G and extended the maturity of its revolving credit facility as part of a broader refinancing program affecting more than $1.25 billion of debt. The new term loan matures July 15, 2030.
The post Gray Media Closes $600 Million Term Loan And Extends $680 Million Revolver appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Gray Media Closes $600 Million Term Loan And Extends $680 Million Revolver
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Gray Media Closes $600 Million Term Loan And Extends $680 Million Revolver
Gray Media closed a new $600 million Term Loan G and extended the maturity of its revolving credit facility as part of a broader refinancing program affecting more than $1.25 billion of debt. The new term loan matures July 15, 2030.
It was priced at 350 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate and issued at a 0.5% original issue discount.
Gray also reduced its existing $750 million revolving credit facility to $680 million.
The revolver’s maturity was extended from December 1, 2028 to July 15, 2030.
Proceeds from Term Loan G were used to repay part of Gray’s Term Loan D due December 1, 2028.
Following the repayment, approximately $150 million of Term Loan D remains outstanding.
The refinancing follows Gray’s August 2026 issuance of $750 million of 7.5% senior secured first-lien notes due 2034.
Proceeds from that issuance were used in part to repay $675 million of 10.5% first-lien notes due 2029.
Gray said the transactions collectively extended maturities on more than $1.25 billion of debt and lowered overall borrowing costs.
The company now has no material debt maturities until after both the 2026 and 2028 political election cycles.
Its nearest maturities are the remaining $150 million of Term Loan D due in December 2028 and $350 million of notes due in July 2029.

articles.title: Blue Bird Secures $600 Million Credit Facility Led By BMO And Bank Of America
articles.snippet:
Blue Bird has completed a $600 million senior secured credit facility refinancing that more than doubles its committed borrowing capacity and extends its debt maturity to September 2031.
The post Blue Bird Secures $600 Million Credit Facility Led By BMO And Bank Of America appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Blue Bird Secures $600 Million Credit Facility Led By BMO And Bank Of America
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Blue Bird Secures $600 Million Credit Facility Led By BMO And Bank Of America
Blue Bird has completed a $600 million senior secured credit facility refinancing that more than doubles its committed borrowing capacity and extends its debt maturity to September 2031.
The new financing replaces Blue Bird’s previous $250 million credit facilities, which were scheduled to mature in November 2028.
The refinancing consists of a $300 million revolving credit facility and a $300 million delayed draw term loan.
Borrowings under the delayed draw term loan are available for up to 24 months after closing or until the entire $300 million has been drawn.
Blue Bird can use the term loan to refinance existing debt and primarily fund capital projects, research and development and working capital.
At closing, the school bus manufacturer had approximately $86 million of carry-over debt drawn under the new facilities and more than $670 million of available liquidity.
The refinancing also reduces Blue Bird’s borrowing costs.
The interest-rate margin is now SOFR plus 1.25% to 2.25%, depending on leverage, compared with SOFR plus 1.75% to 3.25% under the previous facilities.
The agreement also eliminates the prior 0.10% credit spread adjustment.
Blue Bird’s maximum total net leverage ratio increases to 3.25 times, with a temporary 0.50-times step-up for four quarters after a qualifying acquisition of at least $75 million.
The accordion feature has also been expanded to the greater of $250 million or one times trailing 12-month EBITDA, with additional capacity available subject to a leverage test.
BMO served as administrative agent, joint lead arranger and joint bookrunner.
Bank of America served as syndication agent, joint lead arranger and joint bookrunner.
CIBC Bank USA, Fifth Third Bank, Regions Bank and TD Bank also served as joint lead arrangers and joint bookrunners.
KEY QUOTES:
“While Blue Bird already has a very strong balance sheet, this refinancing more than doubles our available borrowing capacity, lowers our cost of debt and extends maturity out to 2031. It gives us the flexibility to continue to invest in our operations and product development, while maintaining a conservative balance sheet. We appreciate the strong support from our bank group, led by BMO.”
Razvan Radulescu, Chief Financial Officer of Blue Bird

articles.snippet:
Penguin Solutions reported record fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net sales of $566.7 million, up 68% from $337.9 million in the prior-year period.

articles.text:
Penguin Solutions: Q4 Revenue Jumps 68% To Record $567 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Penguin Solutions: Q4 Revenue Jumps 68% To Record $567 Million As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
Penguin Solutions reported record fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net sales of $566.7 million, up 68% from $337.9 million in the prior-year period.
Operating income increased 458% to $69.5 million.
Non-GAAP operating income rose 129% to $89.8 million.
Net income increased to $93.2 million from $9.4 million a year earlier, representing growth of 888%.
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $93 million from the prior-year period.
Diluted earnings per share increased to $1.29 from $0.11, while non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to $1 from $0.43.
Penguin said performance accelerated during the second half of fiscal 2026 following the launch of its AI Factory Platform and a greater focus on AI-driven data center demand.
Revenue growth accelerated from relatively flat levels during the first half to 48% in the third quarter and 68% in the fourth quarter.
For full-year fiscal 2026, Penguin generated $1.73 billion in net sales, up 26%.
Annual operating income increased 185% to approximately $166 million.
Net income reached $181 million, up 611%, while adjusted EBITDA increased 37% to a record $256 million.
Full-year diluted EPS was $2.60 compared with $0.28 in the prior year, while non-GAAP diluted EPS increased 51% to $2.87.
Penguin added six AI Infrastructure data center customers during the fourth quarter, including four neocloud providers.
Across fiscal 2026, the company added 17 new AI Infrastructure customers, while 12 existing customers expanded their business with Penguin.
One new customer selected Penguin to deploy and operate a 36,000-GPU AI factory in Norway and has $10 billion in contracted compute from a major AI lab.
Another publicly traded neocloud customer with more than $3 billion in signed multi-year contracts selected Penguin for AI infrastructure deployment and 24/7 operations services.
Penguin also advanced its ClusterWareAI platform with self-managing agentic AI capabilities that can automatically detect and remediate GPU performance issues.
The company closed an oversubscribed $750 million convertible senior notes offering due 2031 carrying a 0% coupon.
Based on accelerating AI Infrastructure demand, Penguin raised its fiscal 2027 outlook.
The company now expects approximately $2.43 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue at the midpoint, representing roughly 40% growth, plus or minus 10 percentage points.
Penguin also expects GAAP diluted EPS of approximately $3.50 and non-GAAP diluted EPS of approximately $4.45, representing year-over-year growth of roughly 35% and 55%, respectively.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our company performance accelerated significantly in the second half of fiscal 2026 following the launch of our AI Factory Platform and increased focus on the data center market.”
Kash Shaikh, President and CEO of Penguin Solutions
“The proof is in the results. After relatively flat year-over-year net sales in the first half, growth accelerated to 48% in Q3 and 68% in Q4, driving second-half growth of 58%.”
Kash Shaikh, President and CEO of Penguin Solutions
“As we enter fiscal 2027, our memory business remains strong, and our AI Infrastructure business is accelerating further.”
Kash Shaikh, President and CEO of Penguin Solutions

articles.title: WhiteHawk Leads $560 Million Financing For Bally’s Bronx Development
articles.snippet:
WhiteHawk Capital Partners led a $560 million senior secured credit facility supporting Bally's planned $4 billion casino and entertainment development in the Bronx. WhiteHawk is serving as agent and lead lender for the financing.
The post WhiteHawk Leads $560 Million Financing For Bally’s Bronx Development appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
WhiteHawk Leads $560 Million Financing For Bally’s Bronx Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
WhiteHawk Leads $560 Million Financing For Bally’s Bronx Development
WhiteHawk Capital Partners led a $560 million senior secured credit facility supporting Bally’s planned $4 billion casino and entertainment development in the Bronx. WhiteHawk is serving as agent and lead lender for the financing.
The facility includes $400 million of term loan commitments available at closing and another $160 million of delayed-draw term loan commitments.
Proceeds will support pre-construction expenses and development costs related to Bally’s Bronx.
The financing also provides additional liquidity for general corporate purposes.
Bally’s Bronx is planned as an integrated gaming, hospitality, and entertainment destination at Ferry Point.
Plans include a casino, 500-room hotel, event venue, restaurants, supporting infrastructure, and an 18-hole championship golf course.
Bally’s was one of three gaming companies awarded New York City-area casino licenses on December 15, 2025.
The other projects are Hard Rock Metropolitan Park in Queens near Citi Field and Resorts World New York City at Aqueduct Racetrack.
The financing is intended to support Bally’s through design, permitting, and other development work as the company prepares to arrange comprehensive construction financing.
DLA Piper served as legal advisor to WhiteHawk.
KEY QUOTES:
“This financing gives Bally’s the capital to advance design, permitting and other critical development activities as it prepares for the next phase of the Bronx project.”
Bob Louzan, Managing Partner at WhiteHawk Capital Partners
“WhiteHawk has proven their ability to execute complicated financings in tight timeframes and in doing so has proven themselves a fantastic capital partner for our Bally’s New York project.”
Soo Kim, Chairman of Bally’s Corporation

articles.title: Bally’s Closes $560 Million Financing Led By WhiteHawk For $4 Billion Bronx Casino Project
articles.snippet:
Bally's Corporation has closed financing led by WhiteHawk Capital Partners to support development of its planned $4 billion Bally's Bronx integrated casino project in New York.
The post Bally’s Closes $560 Million Financing Led By WhiteHawk For $4 Billion Bronx Casino Project appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Bally’s Closes $560 Million Financing Led By WhiteHawk For $4 Billion Bronx Casino Project
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Bally’s Closes $560 Million Financing Led By WhiteHawk For $4 Billion Bronx Casino Project
Bally’s Corporation has closed financing led by WhiteHawk Capital Partners to support development of its planned $4 billion Bally’s Bronx integrated casino project in New York.
The financing includes $400 million of term loans funded at closing and another $160 million of delayed-draw term loan commitments that remain available for future draws.
Bally’s plans to use the initial $400 million primarily for pre-construction costs and expenditures associated with Bally’s Bronx.
A portion of the proceeds will also be available for general corporate purposes, including transaction fees and expenses related to the financing.
The $160 million delayed-draw facility is intended to support continued development of the Bronx project as construction advances.
Bally’s expects the integrated resort to open by 2030.
Plans call for approximately 3 million square feet of gaming facilities, a 500-room hotel, a 2,000-person event center and an 18-hole golf course.
The company was awarded a license to develop the full-scale casino and resort in the Bronx and is separately developing an integrated destination resort in Chicago.
WhiteHawk Capital Partners is a private credit investment manager focused on asset-based financing for middle-market public and private companies.
Support: Citizens Capital Markets & Advisory served as financial adviser to Bally’s, while Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson served as legal adviser.

articles.snippet: US-Based Legal AI Startup Harvey Raises $550 Million at $15.5 Billion Valuation بوابة التكنولوجيا المالية
articles.text:
US-Based Legal AI Startup Harvey Raises $550 Million at $15.5 Billion Valuation
فنتيك جيت: مصطفي عيد
الإثنين 12/أكتوبر/2026 - 08:46 م

شارك
Harvey, a US-based artificial intelligence company developing AI solutions for the legal industry, has raised $550 million in a funding round that values the company at $15.5 billion, with the investment co-led by Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners.
Announced on September 9, 2026, the funding will support Harvey’s efforts to help law firms, in-house legal departments and professional services firms develop, manage and own their institutional intelligence at scale, as organizations increasingly adopt artificial intelligence to improve legal workflows and strengthen their competitive advantage.
The latest investment follows the introduction of Harvey’s first post-trained open-weight AI model and the launch of Harvey LAB, the company’s Legal Agent Benchmark, as it expands its technology and capabilities for legal professionals.
The funding round brought together existing investors, including Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Coatue, Conviction, Elad Gil, Evantic, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Verified Capital and WNDR. New investors participating in the round include Diffusion, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sapphire Ventures and Whale Rock.
Harvey’s co-founders, Winston Weinberg and Gabe Pereyra, said the opportunity for businesses to strengthen their competitive advantage through AI has reached an important stage, adding that the company aims to become a global partner for legal teams seeking to advance their AI capabilities.
The co-founders also said Harvey plans to recruit and develop a leading team in the sector to support clients through the next phase of AI-driven transformation.
Harvey has established a presence among major law firms, with 80% of firms in the Am Law 100 using its platform. Its customer base also includes leading in-house legal teams at some of the world’s largest companies, including five of the Fortune 10.
The new funding strengthens Harvey’s position in the legal AI market as it continues developing tools designed to help legal professionals use AI across their operations while building and retaining control over their institutional knowledge and intelligence.

articles.title: Legal AI Legora Raises $550M Series E at $8.8B Valuation
articles.snippet: Legal AI Legora Raises $550M Series E at $8.8B Valuation Wowtale
articles.text:
Legal teams aren’t treating AI as a mere assistant anymore. Instead of help on individual tasks like contract review or case research, they’re handing entire multi-step workflows to agents. Legora has pushed that shift harder than most legal AI companies. In-house legal teams made up only a small slice of its customer base a year ago; in the third quarter of this year, they accounted for more than 40% of new customers. In the US, now Legora’s largest market by revenue, more than half of the AmLaw 50 are customers — a striking footprint given the company only opened its first US office in spring 2025.
Legora calls itself the agentic operating system for legal professionals. The pitch is to embed AI across the three high-stakes, time-consuming tasks that fill a lawyer’s day: sifting through mountains of documents for what matters, researching case law and statutes, and drafting contracts and opinions. Founded in Stockholm in 2023, Legora launched its platform in October 2024 and now has more than 1,000 employees across 18 offices, serving more than 140,000 legal professionals at over 2,400 law firms and in-house legal teams in more than 80 markets. The new funding will support expansion across North America — where Legora has offices in New York, Denver, Chicago, Houston, San Francisco, Toronto, and Mexico City — along with Europe and Asia-Pacific, and will deepen investment in the Legora aOS, including new agentic intake, horizon-scanning, and legal-research products.
Founder and CEO Max Junestrand had no legal background when he started the company. The idea came from watching a friend who’d just joined a law firm spend an entire summer summarizing court rulings — prompting the question of why people were doing by hand what software could already handle. Junestrand holds a master’s in computer science with a focus on machine learning from Sweden’s KTH Royal Institute of Technology, a business degree from the Stockholm School of Economics, and a master’s in engineering from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and passed through McKinsey and venture capital along the way — giving up a promising esports career to found the company instead.
Without any legal-industry connections, he embedded himself for months inside Mannheimer Swartling, the largest law firm in the Nordics, observing lawyers’ actual workflows and iterating on the product on the spot. Co-founders Sigge Labor and August Erséus joined him. “The opportunity in legal is enormous and we are still early,” Junestrand said. “AI is changing the role of the lawyer… and it is reshaping how law firms and in-house legal teams are organized and how their work gets done. We chose investors who share our long-term view and know what it takes to build a lasting company.”
CFO David Eckstein added: “Growth only counts if the business underneath it holds up. We have passed $200 million in ARR, and we want every dollar of it to be a durable one.”
Legora said it raised a $550 million Series E at an $8.8 billion post-money valuation . Atreides Management led the round, with new investors Baron Capital, Capital Group, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Glade Brook Capital Partners, and J.P. Morgan. Every major existing investor also returned, including Accel, Benchmark, Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst, ICONIQ, Insight Partners, Menlo Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and Sands Capital. articles.title: NETSTREIT Secures $550 Million In New Term Loan Commitments And Amends Facilities
articles.snippet:
NETSTREIT has closed $550 million in additional financing commitments and amended existing credit facilities agented by PNC Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist Bank.
The post NETSTREIT Secures $550 Million In New Term Loan Commitments And Amends Facilities appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
NETSTREIT Secures $550 Million In New Term Loan Commitments And Amends Facilities
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
NETSTREIT Secures $550 Million In New Term Loan Commitments And Amends Facilities
NETSTREIT has closed $550 million in additional financing commitments and amended existing credit facilities agented by PNC Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist Bank.
The additional financing is being provided through an amendment to NETSTREIT’s term loan agreement agented by PNC Bank.
The commitments include a $100 million increase to the REIT’s existing senior unsecured 5.5-year term loan facility. The full amount was funded at closing.
NETSTREIT also received a $50 million increase to its existing senior unsecured seven-year term loan facility, which was also fully funded at closing.
The largest component is a new $400 million senior unsecured seven-year delayed-draw term loan facility. The facility was undrawn at closing and can be drawn through September 28, 2027.
NETSTREIT used proceeds from the two incremental term loans, together with a remaining $50 million draw under its existing 2032 term loan, to repay its $200 million term loan that had been scheduled to mature in February 2028.
Interest rate swaps previously associated with the repaid term loan remain in place and continue fixing the interest rate on an equivalent amount of borrowings through February 2028.
The company also amended its PNC term loan agreement and credit agreements agented by PNC, Wells Fargo and Truist. Some of the amendments reduce applicable margin spreads.
NETSTREIT said the transactions extend its weighted-average debt maturity profile and leave the company with no material debt maturities until early 2029.
The financing also addresses a significant portion of NETSTREIT’s anticipated debt capital requirements through 2027 and increases available liquidity.
PNC Capital Markets, Huntington National Bank, Truist Securities, Capital One and Regions Capital Markets served as joint lead arrangers for the $100 million incremental term loan.
Those firms were joined by TD Bank and U.S. Bank as joint lead arrangers for the $50 million incremental facility.
The $400 million delayed-draw facility includes PNC Capital Markets, Huntington, Capital One, Regions, TD Bank, Manufacturers and Traders Trust Company, Truist Securities and U.S. Bank as joint lead arrangers.
PNC Capital Markets served as sole bookrunner for the 2031 and 2032 incremental term loans and as one of the joint bookrunners for the 2033 delayed-draw facility.
Morrison & Foerster represented NETSTREIT, while Alston & Bird represented the administrative agents.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased with the closing of our $550.0 million in additional term loan commitments and the full repayment of our 2028 term loan. With these transactions, we have meaningfully extended our weighted average debt maturity profile and have no material debt maturing until early 2029. This additional financing also largely addresses our debt capital needs through 2027 and greatly enhances our liquidity position heading into next year. We sincerely appreciate the continued commitment and support of our trusted banking partners,”
Dan Donlan, Chief Financial Officer of NETSTREIT

ID Finance Secures €545 Million as Plazo Targets €200 Million Credit Portfolio in Spain
Vasundhra Tewari
| October 13 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Barcelona-based fintech ID Finance has secured fresh debt and equity financing to expand its consumer lending operations and accelerate the growth of Plazo , its buy now, pay later platform.
Barcelona-based financial technology company ID Finance has secured €545 million in debt and equity financing, marking a significant step in its plans to expand Plazo, its consumer credit platform in Spain.
The financing involves Spice Expeditions, WashU, Kingsway Capital and i80 Group. While the company has not disclosed how much of the total comes from debt and how much from equity, the funding has two distinct purposes. The equity investment will support Plazo’s expansion, while asset-backed financing from i80 Group will help increase its credit portfolio.
The deal comes as ID Finance looks beyond the short-term lending business on which it built its name. Its next phase centres on Plazo, a platform that combines consumer financial services with flexible payment options.
The company is pursuing that expansion after reporting €243 million in group revenue for 2025. Plazo also reached profitability that year, giving ID Finance a stronger financial foundation as it prepares to scale.
Plazo’s €200 Million Credit Portfolio Ambition
One of the central goals behind the financing is to expand Plazo’s lending capacity.
ID Finance expects Plazo’s credit portfolio to reach approximately €200 million in 2026. The platform currently serves more than 400,000 users and has a reported loan book of €137 million.
Plazo’s recent performance offers some insight into why investors are backing its expansion. According to the company, the platform tripled its credit portfolio in 2025, increased revenue by 300% and became profitable.
From Deutsche Bank Backgrounds to a Growing Spanish Fintech
ID Finance is led by co-founders Boris Batine , its CEO, and Alexander Dunaev, its COO, both of whom previously worked at Deutsche Bank.
Batine’s professional experience also includes Renaissance Capital and the Royal Bank of Scotland, while Dunaev previously headed structured products for Central and Eastern Europe at Deutsche Bank.
The company traces its beginnings to 2012 and has developed a substantial consumer lending operation in Spain.
Its Spanish lending platform has more than 3.7 million registered users. During the first six months of 2026, the business issued over €190 million in loans and generated approximately €100 million in revenue.
Although short-term loans remain an important part of its operations, ID Finance has been broadening its product offering through Plazo, which launched in 2021.
The latest funding illustrates how the business is directing more resources towards a platform that aims to provide everyday financial services alongside consumer credit.
Turrón Brings Interest-Free Instalments to Plazo Users
A key part of Plazo’s expansion is Turrón, a financial product introduced in July 2026.
Turrón combines an electronic money account and debit card with a buy now, pay later facility. Eligible purchases can be divided into interest-free instalments at participating merchants, including online stores and physical retail locations.
According to ID Finance, the product does not charge maintenance fees or subscription costs.

articles.title: Sui’s Hashi Bitcoin Finance Network Launches With More Than $500 Million Committed
articles.snippet: Sui’s Hashi Bitcoin Finance Network Launches With More Than $500 Million Committed TradingView
articles.text:
News

Sui’s Hashi Bitcoin Finance Network Launches With More Than $500 Million Committed
2 min read
SUIUSD BTCUSD
TL;DR: Hashi, Sui’s native Bitcoin finance infrastructure, will begin a phased mainnet rollout later this month with more than $500 million in committed capital. Anchorage Digital has joined the launch coalition, giving institutional clients routes into Hashi through qualified custody and self-custody infrastructure.
Sui is preparing to bring its Bitcoin finance system to mainnet with something most new DeFi products do not have on day one: half a billion dollars of capital already lined up.
The Sui Foundation said Thursday that Hashi will begin a phased mainnet rollout later this month backed by more than $500 million in capital commitments from its launch coalition.
Anchorage Digital is also joining that coalition as a launch partner.
Hashi is designed to let Bitcoin remain secured on the Bitcoin network while being used as collateral inside financial applications built on Sui.
When BTC enters the system, a corresponding hBTC asset is minted on Sui. That hBTC can then interact with lending markets, vaults and other applications. When the position is unwound, hBTC is burned and the underlying Bitcoin is released.
The distinction between that model and a conventional wrapped Bitcoin token is central to the pitch.
Hashi is attempting to give institutions a way to use BTC as programmable collateral without treating Bitcoin as something that first has to be sold or permanently moved into a separate smart-contract ecosystem.
The $500 million commitment gives those markets a meaningful starting point.
Sui says the initial capital will support lending, borrowing, credit products, vaults, structured products and other Bitcoin-backed applications as individual providers complete their integrations.
The coalition already includes names such as BitGo, Bullish, Cumberland, FalconX and Ledger.
Anchorage adds another important route into the system.
Institutional clients will be able to access Hashi through Anchorage’s Atlas infrastructure for tri-party collateral arrangements while maintaining qualified custody. A second route will use Porto, Anchorage’s institutional self-custody wallet, for firms that want more direct access.
That makes the launch particularly relevant to public companies and funds holding large Bitcoin positions.
Bitcoin treasury companies have accumulated enormous balances, but turning those holdings into working capital usually means selling BTC, borrowing through a centralized lender or entering bespoke financing arrangements.
Hashi is trying to create on-chain alternatives.
The security model will face scrutiny precisely because the amounts involved are potentially large.
Sui says Hashi uses a 2-of-2 multisignature structure involving validators and a guardian layer, with additional controls designed to slow or stop suspicious movements. Its smart contracts have undergone formal verification and the underlying cryptographic protocol has been reviewed.
Those safeguards do not remove risk, but they show the product is being built for a different audience from the early days of experimental Bitcoin DeFi.
